site.name: codekite
site.summary: codekite-clone Fictional cloud CI/CD service "CodeKite CI" marketing site, focused on the pricing-page usage calculator. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Short landing: hero (YAML code example on the right), 3 feature cards, CTA to pricing | | `pricing.html` | Main page: 3 plan cards (Free / Team / Enterprise) + usage calculator (three slider+number pairs linked two-way: build minutes / concurrency / storage + ARM / macOS / GPU runner checkboxes); right-side sticky monthly total + recommended-plan badge + line-item cost breakdown; below: 16-row plan comparison table; 10-question FAQ accordion; trusted-logo row; 4-column footer | | `docs.html` | Placeholder quickstart page (one YAML example) |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full codekite system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The CodeKite pricing page features a functional usage calculator but suffers from critical accessibility and mobile usability issues. The primary friction points are tiny tap targets for runner checkboxes (13x13px) on mobile, missing accessible labels for all calculator inputs, and broken conversion paths where key CTAs lead to dead ends (#). Additionally, the calculator logic exhibits inconsistencies, recommending high-tier plans even when usage is zeroed out.

exploration_plan.goal: Evaluate the UX of the CodeKite pricing calculator and adjacent marketing pages, focusing on the usability of the cost estimation tool, plan comparison clarity, and mobile responsiveness.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will start on the landing page to verify navigation and value proposition, then move to the Pricing page for an exhaustive test of the usage calculator (sliders, inputs, checkboxes) and plan selection logic. It will conclude with a check of the Docs page and a full mobile viewport regression to address known tap-target issues.
assumptions: The 'Sign in' link (#) is a placeholder and will not lead to a functional authentication flow.
The pricing calculator updates the 'Monthly Total' and 'Recommended Plan' dynamically via client-side JavaScript without page reloads.
Footer links like 'Changelog', 'Status', and 'Security' are likely placeholders or empty anchors based on the prescan.
risk_hotspots: pricing.html: Usage Calculator - Two-way binding between sliders and number inputs must be smooth and accurate.
pricing.html: Runner Checkboxes - ARM/macOS/GPU toggles must correctly adjust the per-minute rate in the breakdown.
Global: Mobile Navigation - Prescan indicates small tap targets (<44px) which may fail accessibility/usability checks on mobile.

phases.title: Landing Page & Navigation
phases.objective: Validate the initial user journey, hero messaging, and primary CTAs.
key_checks: Verify Hero section YAML code snippet is readable.
Click 'See pricing' CTA and confirm navigation to pricing.html.
Click 'Read docs' CTA and confirm navigation to docs.html.
Check footer links for broken states or empty anchors.
exit_criteria: Successfully navigated to Pricing and Docs pages from Index.
No console errors during initial load.

phases.title: Pricing Calculator Core Logic
phases.objective: Stress-test the interactive cost estimator for accuracy and usability.
key_checks: Interact with 'Build minutes' slider: Verify number input updates and total cost recalculates.
Interact with 'Concurrent builds' slider: Verify impact on recommended plan badge.
Type directly into number inputs: Verify sliders update correspondingly (two-way binding).
Toggle 'ARM', 'macOS', and 'GPU' runner checkboxes: Verify line-item cost breakdown updates immediately.
Test edge cases: Set values to 0 and maximums to check for UI overflow or negative costs.
exit_criteria: Recommended plan badge switches logically (e.g., Free -> Team -> Enterprise) based on usage.
No visual overlap of calculator elements.

phases.title: Plan Comparison & Content
phases.objective: Ensure static content (plans, FAQ, table) is legible and accessible.
key_checks: Review the 3 plan cards (Free, Team, Enterprise) for clear hierarchy.
Expand/Collapse multiple items in the FAQ accordion to check for layout shifts.
Scan the 16-row plan comparison table for readability and alignment.
Verify 'Start free trial' and 'Talk to sales' buttons are distinct and clickable.
exit_criteria: FAQ accordion functions without breaking layout.
Comparison table is readable on desktop.

phases.title: Docs & Recovery Paths
phases.objective: Validate the secondary content page and return paths.
key_checks: Verify YAML quickstart example is visible and formatted correctly.
Use global navigation to return to Pricing and Index pages.
Attempt to click 'Sign in' to confirm it does not crash the browser (expected no-op).
exit_criteria: Navigation loop (Index <-> Pricing <-> Docs) works seamlessly.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Regression
phases.objective: Identify usability issues specific to touch devices, focusing on the prescan warnings.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport (e.g., iPhone SE/12).
Attempt to tap nav links ('Product', 'Pricing', 'Docs') to verify if hit areas are too small.
Test the Pricing Calculator sliders on touch: Ensure they are draggable and not obscured by other elements.
Check if the sticky monthly total overlaps content when scrolling on mobile.
Verify the plan comparison table handles horizontal overflow gracefully (scroll vs. break).
exit_criteria: Critical mobile interactions (nav, calculator) are possible, even if difficult.
Layout does not break horizontally on small screens.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit index.html, pricing.html, and docs.html at least once.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all 3 calculator sliders, 3 runner checkboxes, and 2 number inputs on the pricing page.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat Phase 2 (Calculator) and Phase 1 (Nav) on mobile viewport.

notes: Pay close attention to the 'missing_input_label' warnings from the prescan on the pricing page; visually verify if inputs are adequately described for accessibility.
The 'Sign in' link is a dead end (#); do not spend steps trying to recover from it beyond confirming it doesn't error out.

findings.user_goal: Configure add-on runners (ARM, macOS, GPU) on a mobile device.
findings.problem: The checkboxes for selecting specialized runners have tap targets of only 13x13px, significantly below the recommended 44x44px minimum for touch interfaces.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in steps-67-72 and final_observation identify 'Linux ARM runners' (ux-13), 'macOS runners' (ux-14), and 'GPU runners' (ux-15) as having 13x13px bounding boxes. This makes them extremely difficult to hit accurately on touch screens, leading to frustration and mis-taps.
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users will struggle to select these high-value add-ons, likely abandoning the configuration or feeling the interface is broken. This directly impacts revenue potential from mobile-administered accounts.
findings.suggestion: Increase the clickable area of the checkbox labels to at least 44x44px. Ensure the text label itself is part of the clickable target, not just the small visual box.

findings.user_goal: Use screen readers or keyboard navigation to operate the pricing calculator.
findings.problem: All range sliders and number inputs in the 'Estimate your monthly cost' section lack associated labels, aria-labels, or placeholders.
findings.evidence: Multiple layout warnings (final_observation, steps-01-06) flag 'missing_input_label' for ux-7 through ux-12. Screen reader users would hear generic input types without context (e.g., 'edit text' instead of 'Build minutes per month').
findings.why_it_matters: This violates WCAG guidelines and excludes users with disabilities from independently estimating costs, creating a significant trust and compliance gap.
findings.suggestion: Add visible <label> elements linked via 'for' attributes to each input, or include descriptive aria-labels (e.g., aria-label='Build minutes per month') for each slider and number field.

findings.user_goal: Start a trial or purchase a plan after reviewing pricing.
findings.problem: Primary Call-to-Action buttons ('Start free trial', 'Start trial', 'Talk to sales') have href='#' or lead to no action, resulting in dead-end clicks.
findings.evidence: Steps-19-24 noted that clicking 'Start trial' (ux-8) resulted in no navigation. Final observation shows 'Start free trial' (ux-3) and 'Talk to sales' (ux-6) also point to '#' or have no valid destination. This breaks the core conversion funnel.
findings.why_it_matters: Users interested in converting are blocked immediately. This creates a perception of an unfinished or broken product, causing immediate drop-off.
findings.suggestion: Connect these buttons to actual sign-up flows, contact forms, or calendar scheduling tools. If the feature is coming soon, disable the button or provide a clear 'Coming Soon' tooltip.

findings.user_goal: Understand why a specific plan is recommended based on their usage.
findings.problem: The calculator recommends 'Enterprise' or 'Team' plans even when all usage inputs (minutes, concurrency, storage) are set to 0.
findings.evidence: In steps-73-78, after setting all inputs to 0, the reflection notes the calculator still recommended 'Enterprise' with the message 'workload over Team caps', which is logically inconsistent for zero usage. The expected behavior is a recommendation for the 'Free' plan.
findings.why_it_matters: This erodes trust in the calculator's accuracy. Users may suspect hidden fees or believe the tool is rigged to upsell them, rather than providing an honest estimate.
findings.suggestion: Review the recommendation logic to ensure that 0 usage correctly maps to the 'Free' tier. Provide clear tooltips explaining exactly which metric triggered the upgrade recommendation.
findings.source_hint: pricing.html: Calculator Logic / Recommended Plan Badge

findings.user_goal: Navigate the site on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Global navigation links ('Docs', 'Pricing') have tap targets smaller than 44px height (e.g., 21px height).
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in steps-01-06 and final_observation highlight 'Docs' (ux-2) and other nav links as having heights around 21px, failing mobile touch target guidelines.
findings.why_it_matters: While less critical than the calculator issues, this adds cumulative friction to basic site navigation on mobile, making the entire experience feel unpolished.
findings.suggestion: Add padding to the navigation link containers to ensure the total clickable height is at least 44px.
